## Separate final-wave root decisions

These 14 decisions follow the preserved historical appendix. They do not alter its original 42 ordered lines.

1. Complete native direct work can fully pass. Sequential substitution remains reduced, and independent methods retain action permissions and structured receipts. This corrects the blanket worker assumption without granting host setup. The cost is a coordinated contract migration.
2. One implementer owns this entire wave. Local F4 and report commits provide real identities before the one scoped review of the full range. The cost is a fourth freeze and 210 blocked identity relinks; no pass transfers.
3. Installed loading, discovery, invocation, caches and installed rollback remain unverified because separate authorization and access are absent. Source proof cannot supply them.
4. Live forge and external actions remain outside scope. Injected watcher tests establish local behavior only; the stack cap needs an explicit completeness boundary.
5. Network fetching and live product update, acceptance or rollback remain unverified. Full-package inert transactions are authorized, with their fixture-only limits.
6. New dependency setup, lifecycle execution, global changes and runtime substitutions remain unauthorized. Reading the existing exact approved snapshot permits local checks only.
7. Actual workers, model diversity, scheduling, cancellation, cross-session recovery, live apps and sustained performance still need host observations. Synthetic receipts check contracts only.
8. Benny connectors, media, secrets, triggers, compensation and delivery require grants that are absent. Their static contracts and explicit blocks remain.
9. External-document liveness, Wiki publication and rendered aesthetics remain outside local review. Saved official-source evidence supports setup wording only; local artwork inspection supports descriptive alt text.
10. Power loss, forced termination, failed backups, hostile concurrent replacement and atomic multi-file reader visibility remain excluded recovery properties. Caught-failure fixtures do not establish them.
11. The watcher rejects open-PR counts at or above 300 and treats UNKNOWN as bounded status unavailable. Large repositories or prolonged unknown state may remain blocked or time out.
12. Full-package apply needs a hash-bound reviewed metadata bundle. It validates projected closure before writes and retains old fragment provenance. New or removed workflows need supplied ownership, cases, catalog and dependencies; no observations are synthesized.
13. Inert ignored .upstream review sources and drafts are excluded from operative scanning. Runtime destinations and operative links into them are rejected. This fixes 471 false errors without a broad exemption.
14. Every forge BLOCKED state refuses readiness even with a successful head rollup. The explicit forge-blocked merge gate avoids falsely claiming individual failed checks. This is a deliberate tightening of inherited behavior; other documented known MERGEABLE states retain independent gates.

## Preserved watch-pr test incident

Implementation unit 14 initially ran `bun --no-install test skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/github.test.ts skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/cli.test.ts` before constructor transport injection existed. The canonical reader ignored the fake constructor argument and invoked the real read-only transport. These actual commands were constructed:

```text
gh pr view 42 --repo owner/repo --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,headRefOid,headRefName,baseRefName,state,mergedAt,isDraft
gh pr list --repo owner/repo --state open --limit 300 --json number,headRefName,baseRefName
gh pr checks 42 --repo owner/repo --json name,state,description,link,workflow,bucket
```

The checks command ran twice. View and list reported that GraphQL could not resolve owner/repo. Checks returned unusable results; the duplicate-action assertion passed vacuously because its fake call log was empty. That initial result is INVALID evidence. No credentials were displayed and no merge, comment, push, setup or other external mutation was attempted. The original outputs were in the tool transcript, not a saved scratch log.

After injection, the corrected fake-only policy and transport run passed 46 tests with 138 assertions. The exact command was `bun --no-install test skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/policy.test.ts skills/poteto-mode/scripts/watch-pr/github.test.ts`. Later approved dependency checks and the fresh F3 helper run cover the complete CLI suite. This task did not repeat live gh calls. Successful later tests do not erase the initial boundary violation.
